newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia rural commodity prices fall-NFF/Dresdner.
newsitem.headline: Australia rural commodity prices fall-NFF/Dresdner.

text.p: The National Farmers' Federation-Dresdner Australia Ltd rural commodity price index fell by 2.1 percent in July in Special Drawing Rights (SDR) terms, Dresdner chief economist Rob Henderson said.

The fall was largely due to commodity prices receiving a significant jolt in early July with the plunge in the price of gold after the sell-off of two-thirds of the Reserve Bank of Australia's reserves. The overall Dresdner SDR index is now only 1.1 percent higher than at the same time last year.
"The gold price fell heavily during early July but recovered some of the lost ground late in the month," Henderson said.
The rural SDR index decreased 2.9 percent and is 2.4 percent above the level of a year ago, NFF director of economic policy Todd Ritchie said.
But in Australian dollar terms, the index fell 2.1 percent and are 3.6 percent higher than a year ago.
"While barley, sorghum, meat and cotton prices strengthened, this was offset by lower prices for wheat, wool and sugar," Ritchie said.
He said the gold market now looked a lot like the wool market, with prices capped until stockpiles were wound down to "appropriate levels".
"It is, however, doubtful that the Europeans will embark on a wholesale sell down of their excess stocks," Henderson said.
In Australian dollar terms, the index fell by 1.4 percent in July compared with June, reflecting a weaker average value, and is now 2.4 percent higher than a year ago.
Non-rural SDR prices fell by 1.7 percent in July and are 0.2 percent lower than the level at the same time a year ago.
However, the NFF and Dresdner said the outlook for commodities remained generally positive on the strength of healthy growth in the United States, Japan and some of the second tier G-7 economies.
